headline: PPI jumps 1.3% m/m, the most since 2022, and $951M is liquidated in 24h, 90% of it longs; yields still fall to 5.08%, ETFs see a preliminary $261M outflow on 10/14, and flows stay weak after the leverage flush.
summary: A second hot inflation print after CPI, plus a slump in Asian tech stocks, pushed BTC below $80K intraday before buyers took it back to close at 86% of the day's range, back inside the value area. Leverage got flushed, but weighted funding is still 7.89% and ETFs flipped to a preliminary outflow on 10/14, so flows have not turned stronger; the market stage stays Bull (day 7), and no exit rule fired or is close. Next: whether ETFs return to inflows, and the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

overview.lead: Bull day 7; two straight hot inflation prints and a large long liquidation, yet price reclaimed the value area after dipping below $80K, and valuation is still mid-cycle. All three lenses say hold, no action.

cycle.lead: Market stage: Bull (since 2026-10-09, day 7); 36 straight closes above a rising 200-day MA (threshold 30).
points: 200-day MA $72,285, above $70,240 thirty days ago and still rising; capitulation has already occurred (2026-06-30, $58,525).

Evidence lights 3/6 (they show strength of evidence only, not part of the rule): MVRV above its 1-year mean (1.514 vs 1.438), realized cap +1.25% over 30 days, and close above short-term holder cost $74,393 (10/09) are on; 12-month momentum (−28.1%), 90-day exchange supply (+0.58%), and short-term holder cost vs true market mean (−6.16%, 10/09) are off.

Readings: extrapolating the last 30 days linearly, short-term holder cost would cross above the true market mean around 12/12; assuming a flat price, 12-month momentum would turn positive around 2027-01-31. Both are assumptions, not forecasts.
By rule, Bull reverts to Bear only after 30 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA; days below now: 0. Tidemark low test: no break of $58,525 before 12/19.

news.title: US September PPI rose 1.3% m/m (expected 0.6%), the most since March 2022, and 6.3% y/y; core +0.7% m/m, +5.0% y/y. The 10-year yield still fell 10.7 bp to close at 5.08%, and October hike odds dropped from 33.2% to 27.1%
news.read: Two hot inflation prints in a row, but bonds caught a safe-haven bid, yields fell, and hike odds went down rather than up; for BTC that is relief after the bad news, not a turn. The site's FRED reads of a 5.19% 10-year and 2.84% real yield (+22 bp over 20 days) are still high, so the high-rate backdrop is unchanged. Short-term macro; it touches neither the 200-day MA nor any exit rule.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs saw a $261.46M net outflow on 10/14: FBTC −$152.73M, IBIT −$110.94M, only BITB +$2.22M
news.read: Farside shows −$261.4M, almost identical, so the site lists it as a preliminary 10/14 value. The prior day's $175.7M inflow was erased in one day, and the seven complete trading days 10/05–10/13 still total −$570.9M; without a run of inflows, flows cannot be called stronger. Realized cap is still +1.25% over 30 days; no change to the market stage or exit framework.

news.title: $951.4M liquidated across crypto in 24h, $876.3M of it longs (CoinGlass); BTC fell as low as $80,764, ETH −6.5%
news.read: About 3× the 10/14 liquidations, with longs at roughly 90%: a clear leverage flush; CoinDesk puts BTC futures liquidations at about $197M. Yet the site's weighted funding is still 7.89% and the risk reversal −2.90, so leverage is neither cleared out nor crowded. Short-term noise; no effect on the cycle view.

news.title: The AI-stock selloff spread to Asia: Korea's KOSPI fell about 8% in a day and about 20% over seven sessions; BTC broke below $80K intraday (first time in a month) before rebounding to $82,000; miner CleanSpark is 60% below its high
news.read: This was a synchronized de-risking across global risk assets, not a crypto-specific problem; the site's BTC–Nasdaq 30-day correlation is 0.664. BTC held $80K and reclaimed the value area, outperforming Asian equities, but miner stocks are tied to the AI compute theme, so miner-side selling is worth watching if the selloff continues; hash ribbons show no capitulation. Short-term backdrop.

news.title: White House crypto council executive director Patrick Witt stepped down on 10/14 with no successor named; the CLARITY Act is still stalled after failing a 49–50 Senate procedural vote on 9/15
news.read: Officially his detail expired, so this is not a policy shift, but the odds of a market-structure bill passing this year are lower. No quantifiable effect on any site indicator; long-term regulatory backdrop.

news.title: The European Banking Authority classified USDC as the first "significant e-money token" under MiCA (first of 45), and will directly supervise its reserves and liquidity from 11/12
news.read: Clearer stablecoin rules help funding rails over the long run; the site's stablecoin supply of $305.5B (+0.6% over 30 days) will not change near term. No direct bearing on the BTC cycle view.

Its ~$78K true market mean and the site's bitcoin-data reading of $79,274 come from different providers and are not subtracted; until $88K is reclaimed it is consolidation, with no change to the market stage or exit framework.
